current_evidence.F9_actual_paragraph: [F9] On a probability space, every square-integrable real random variable $X$ is integrable: $2|X|\le1+X^2$ gives $2\mathbb E|X|\le1+\mathbb E[X^2]<\infty$.

F6_covariance_statement_citation.quote:
Let $X,Y$ be square-integrable real random variables on one probability space.
Then
$$\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathbb E[X^2]-\mathbb E[X]^2,$$
$$\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=\mathbb E[XY]-\mathbb E[X]\mathbb E[Y].$$
Moreover, covariance is symmetric and bilinear on finite linear combinations.
On finite full-power-set probability spaces these formulas reduce to the
published finite identities.

current_evidence.actual_use: 1.3 For centered square-integrable coordinate noises $E_1,E_0$, [F6] and the definitions of variance and covariance give $\operatorname{Var}(E_1-E_0)=\operatorname{Cov}(E_1-E_0,E_1-E_0)$. Bilinearity and symmetry then yield $\sigma_1^2+\sigma_0^2-2c$. Dividing by $h^2$ or $(2h)^2$ gives the forward and central formulas. If the noises are independent with common variance $\sigma^2$, [F9] makes them integrable, so [F7] gives $\mathbb E[E_1E_0]=\mathbb E[E_1]\mathbb E[E_0]=0$; their covariance is $0$ by [F6], yielding $2\sigma^2/h^2$ and $\sigma^2/(2h^2)$.
